summary: Observation of a large luminous shape composed of white and red disks moving across the night sky: probable laser sighting.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named ROSHEIM (67) 22.12.1998, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On December 22, 1998, at approximately 6:05 PM, a witness observed a luminous "serpent" shape in the sky, composed of red and white discs. This luminous shape moved silently "en masse," forming a loop in the sky. The witness observed it for approximately one minute. The witness gave their statement on January 15, 1999, on the advice of a friend. No other statements were collected. It is always very important to start with the witness's interpretation and to take into account any objections they may raise (see the investigation report). - They spontaneously thought of disco spotlights, and the objection arose later when they compared it with photos depicting such lights: "When I first saw this thing, I thought it might be a nightclub light. In the following days, I saw photos of light beams emitted by discotheques, and what I saw on the evening of December 22, 1998, in Rosheim did not correspond to that at all." The witness concludes their statement with: "This is the first time I've observed this kind of phenomenon. Never in my life have I seen anything like this in the sky, except for nightclub lasers." Analysis suggests a high probability of confusion with the impact spots in the sky from ground-based light projectors (like nightclub lasers): - at the time of observation, the phenomenon was new to GEIPAN, but the large number of reports since (see www.geipan.fr, search for cases with Laser or Skyrose phenomena) allows us to affirm that the appearance and movement described by the witness are consistent with the impact spots of these beam projectors on low clouds. - the weather conditions are compatible with the production of spots on a screen of sky (clouds) without the visibility of upward beams. The witness reports a starry sky, which is consistent with the presence of clouds across much of it. Nightclubs were already using projectors, and the pattern and movement of the spots in the sky were achievable with the projector technology of the time. A key element supporting the hypothesis, which the witness himself observed, explains why he rejected this hypothesis (and ultimately testified): the earliest photos available at the time (and the internet was virtually nonexistent) likely depicted laser effects in the sky in their most spectacular form, with upward beams, whereas upward beams are not always visible, and this was probably the case that evening. Although the testimony is relatively complete, with a good description of the UFO and the existence of azimuth readings, it is old (almost 20 years), and it seems difficult to find evidence to confirm the hypothesis so long afterward. Furthermore, measurements of the apparent angular size of the UFO and estimates of its angular height above the horizon are lacking. An on-site investigation at the time would have allowed for further investigation of these points and verification of the existence of a venue (nightclub, community hall, park) capable of using projectors for festive activities on Christmas Eve. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable laser sighting.

summary: Observations of a bright red luminous bar on the eastern horizon; impression of advancing and retreating towards the witnesses: mistaking for a moonrise.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This case, previously classified as D and named SAINT-POURCAIN SUR SIOULE (03) 1998, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On December 5, 1998, at 7:45 PM, a family of three observed a long, luminous horizontal line in the overcast sky, level with the eastern horizon. This line appeared to be composed of bright red globes. After 30 seconds of observation, the UFO appeared to move back and forth before suddenly disappearing. No noise was heard during the observation. Two eyewitness accounts were collected. It was determined that the observation axis was that of the driveway leading to the house. This driveway, rather long (15 m) and narrow (2.5 m), provides a good reference for determining the UFO's azimuth, approximately 65°. Furthermore, the drawing of the UFO above the hedge at the back of the garden allows us to estimate its elevation at around 4°, assuming the observation was made from the middle of the driveway (as the drawing seems to indicate). It so happens that the Moon was precisely in this location in the sky (Stellarium) at 7:45 PM (4° and 66° East). The misinterpretation of the moon is a classic one and can be explained by the cloud cover (present that evening) which almost completely obscured the moon except for small, shifting gaps caused by the wind. These gaps could reproduce all sorts of patterns with one or more lights, generally red when the moon is low below the horizon, as it was that evening. Here, the moon must have been skimming the cloud layer from above or below, since the witness saw the lights outside the cloud mass. The other unusual phenomenon described is the progression of the UFO (Unidentified Flying Object) towards the witnesses and then away from them. This is also a classic misinterpretation; as the gaps vary in size or opacity, the lights vary, and the usual interpretation is to see it as a change in the distance of a light of constant intensity. The witness was contacted by telephone. He confirmed the exact location of his observation in relation to the driveway and the hedges, as well as the height of the hedges at the time. He was able to grasp the mechanisms of misinterpretation described above, and therefore the conclusions of GEIPAN. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as A: Moonrise.

summary: Probable observation of atmospheric reentry
description: On November 17, 1998, at approximately 3:40 a.m., an insomniac observed the sky and noticed the very rapid passage (about one second) of a fireball moving at very high speed. It is likely that this was an atmospheric reentry.

summary: observation of the movement of lights in the sky.
description: Recent report (February 22, 2010) of an earlier observation (October 1998) without a specific date. A witness filmed a series of lights moving across the sky. Unfortunately, the original sound heard by the witness has been replaced with music. No other reports of this phenomenon were collected at that time. The video associated with the report and the questionnaire are unusable, making any investigation impossible. The observation is classified as C.

summary: Observation of a luminous, round, stationary object that then moved off at high speed.
description: On September 27, 1998, at 3:00 AM, a witness observed a round, luminous, yellowish object in the sky. The object was on a hillside and moving very slowly. After about five minutes, the object sped off at high speed before disappearing. No explanation has been given for this phenomenon.

summary: Observation of a green object with a reddish trail.
description: On the evening of September 18, 1998, two witnesses spotted a bright green object in the sky, moving quickly and silently. It abruptly changed course and left a reddish trail behind it. No further information was available.

summary: presence of a large bright spot in the sky.
description: On September 18, 1998, several witnesses observed three aligned points of light, as well as an even brighter globe between the second and third points. The investigation revealed that this was likely the planet Jupiter and three of its moons, which remained in favorable conditions for observation throughout the winter.

summary: observation of a luminous object in the sky; in reality, a night flight of a dirigible for an advertising operation.
description: On September 18, 1998, several witnesses observed a luminous, ovoid object that appeared to follow a precise trajectory. Flashes regularly illuminated the craft. One of the witnesses managed to film the sighting before the craft moved away and disappeared. The investigation revealed that it was a night flight of a Zeppelin-shaped airship used for advertising purposes.

summary: Observation of two bright spots with zigzag trajectories
description: On September 12, 1998, at approximately 9:53 PM, the crew of a flight bound for Dijon observed two bright lights high above them, initially identified as military traffic. However, these lights exhibited a bizarre trajectory, rising and falling and zigzagging frequently. The French Air Force confirmed that no military traffic was present in the area. Furthermore, no radar detection was observed. The investigation failed to identify the nature of this sighting.

summary: Observation of the movement of a helium-filled balloon in the shape of a ladybug.
description: On September 6, 1998, around 8:00 PM, witnesses in their garden spotted a circular object above a tree on a neighboring property. According to the witnesses, this object appeared to be of varying sizes and colors. Several people noted, however, that the object seemed to have legs. Initially stationary above the tree, the object then moved slowly across the sky. One of the witnesses managed to film it for a few minutes before it disappeared completely. A few days later, a person alerted by the press reported to the police that a child's helium balloon, shaped and colored like a ladybug with long legs, had floated away. This balloon, loosely attached to his son's wrist, had floated slowly away in the same area and at the same time the witnesses had spotted the strange object.

summary: Observation of 3 bright points in the sky
description: On August 31, 1998, at approximately 9:30 PM, two witnesses observed three bright points in the sky for about fifteen seconds. No further information is available.

summary: Observations by flight crew of the very rapid passage of 6 very bright points followed by a long luminous trail: observations of an atmospheric reentry of a fireball broken into a meteor procession.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named [AERO AOM] LAT 27.58, LON -33.35 (INT) 26.08.1998, is part of a group of cases recently re-examined. On August 26, 1998, at 12:32 AM, the crew of a DC-10 observed, for approximately 10 seconds, the very rapid passage of six bright points of light with intense visible radiation, leaving behind a long luminous trail. The trajectory was horizontal and straight. The captain, the only witness, wrote a report on August 28, 1998, which was subsequently sent to SEPRA. A sketch representing the UFOs was also drawn by four of the five witnesses, all of which are attached to the report. We can confirm that the observation likely involved the atmospheric reentry of a fireball, which broke up into a meteoric procession (see the investigation report). The horizontal trajectory noted by the witnesses suggests that it could have been a low-angle fireball. However, lacking more data to perform more precise calculations, we cannot determine with certainty whether this fireball actually crossed the Earth's atmosphere or whether it bounced off it, as did the 1972 meteor in the USA. The observation duration, magnitude, and the portion of the sky traversed make this case similar to a low-angle fireball phenomenon that occurred in October 1990. More generally, the witnesses' descriptions fit very well with the hypothesis: white color, straight trajectory, very rapid movement, and the presence of very bright trails. It is surprising that this truly rare and exceptional phenomenon did not receive more attention at the time. However, this fleeting observation (10 seconds) took place in the middle of the Atlantic Ocean, far from any ground-based detection station or visual observers, and was therefore likely witnessed by no one else. The consistency of the account is good, with a detailed testimony, particularly regarding the initial and final positions of the UFOs and their physical description (appearance, magnitude). It is unfortunate, however, that the testimonies of the other crew members are not available. Furthermore, no photographic or video recordings of the phenomenon were made (which is common with such a short duration). Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: observation of meteoroids.

summary: Observation of three bright points in the sky
description: On August 16, 1998, two young boys on vacation at a campsite observed three bright points of light twinkling in the sky and moving at high speed for a few moments. No further information is available.

summary: Observation of a bright point in the sky.
description: On August 14, 1998, at 6:00 AM, a witness observed a bright point in the sky, which he filmed for about thirty minutes. No other information is available.

summary: Observation of bright, colored and sparkling points in the night sky: observation of the star Antares.
description: On August 13, 1998, around midnight, several members of a family observed twinkling lights in the sky. This observation of three bright yellow, red, and green points in the sky corresponded to the star Antares.

summary: Observation of two large white lights and a red triangular light
description: On the night of August 11-12, 1998, at approximately 11:30 PM, a witness saw two large white lights followed by a red light (forming a triangle). No further information is available.

summary: Observations of the passage of an aircraft.
description: On August 10, 1998, around midnight, numerous witnesses, including a train driver, observed a triangular shape in the sky with two red lights and one very bright white light. One witness, based on press reports, indicated that the observed phenomenon was an ultralight aircraft that had also passed near his home during the same time frame. The passage of a Transall aircraft at low altitude, aligned with the two observation points, was also reported. It is therefore almost certain that the observed phenomenon was the passage of one of these two aircraft.

summary: Observation of the slow passage of a luminous sphere in the sky: observation from the Mir space station.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as type C, which are now being re-examined solely to improve the relevance of the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even an explicit change in classification within an investigation report. This particular case study was classified as type C in 1998 by SEPRA, formerly known as Cintegabelle (31), named after the gendarmerie brigade. On August 9, 1998, at 10:10 PM, a couple on their terrace observed the slow, silent, zigzagging passage of a luminous silver sphere across the sky, which then suddenly disappeared. The UFO's trajectory was directed towards the Moon. Another witness in a city several tens of kilometers away reportedly saw this phenomenon but has not been located. The described phenomenon shares many characteristics (duration of observation, shape, size, color, trajectory) with a well-known spacecraft: the Mir space station. Furthermore, Mir was indeed present in the observed area of the sky, although the witnesses did not mention it. At the end of its trajectory, Mir entered the Earth's shadow, marking its visual disappearance, as indicated by the witnesses. It is not the witnesses' visual perception that is at issue, but rather their interpretation of their observation through their emotions (astonishment, fatigue). In the current GEIPAN classification, this case of weak strangeness is classified as UAP A, an observation linked to a misunderstanding with the Mir space station.

summary: Probable aircraft sighting
description: On August 6, 1998, at approximately 10:40 PM, a man in a car was listening to music and looking up at the sky. He then observed a luminous object moving rapidly from south to north. The observation lasted 15 to 20 seconds. An investigation with aviation authorities revealed the passage of a passenger plane and an unidentified radar runway at the time of the observation. The end time of this runway coincided with the time of the witness's observation. While there is no formal proof, it is likely that the witness's observation was of an aircraft.

summary: Probable sightings of MIR space station passes
description: On August 5th and 6th, 1998, around 10:30 PM, a woman observed a white light crossing the sky. The investigation revealed that the MIR space station was clearly visible on both days at the time of the observation. An American experiment involving a remotely piloted, satellite-controlled aircraft was also visible on August 22nd. Based on these observations, the hypothesis that the sighting was of the MIR space station was accepted.

summary: Observation of a bright flash illuminating the entire surface of the sky at night: lack of information.
description: The witness reported in 2013 observing a luminous phenomenon at 1:30 a.m. in August 1998, a kind of flash lasting one or two seconds at most, displaying all colors across the entire sky. The witness's sister also saw the phenomenon. Only one witness account is reported. This account is not usable by GEIPAN (the French National Center for Experimentation on Astronomical Phenomena). Indeed, it is an observation reported 15 years after the event, without specifying the date of the observation. The observation is not unusual, as it suggests a meteorite re-entry flash, but it is impossible to investigate further in this regard. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies this case as C: lack of information.

summary: Recent testimony of an old observation of the low-altitude passage of a dark cylinder with luminous portholes: lack of reliable information.
description: Recent testimony (2014) of an earlier sighting (summer 1998 - the exact date is not given: we are arbitrarily dating it to 01). In July or August 1998, a young boy was playing with another boy on a property in the countryside near CHATEL-MONTAGNE (Allier). Their attention was drawn to an elongated, gray object with portholes (number undetermined) letting in a white light. The object appeared to the right of the chalet in front of them and moved from their right to their left across the clear sky. The main witness described the object as a cylindrical shape, which he estimated to be approximately 50 meters long, with a hard, dark appearance and a coppery color (Pantone 00.36 or 00.45). The object, moving silently, seemed to brush the tops of nearby trees before disappearing a little further away, behind the trees on a hill. The observation lasted between 30 seconds and one minute. The children ran to warn the adults who were outside, turning their backs to the phenomenon and its trajectory. No adult was able to confirm their observation. Only one witness account was collected. The strange experience described the object as cylindrical with portholes that emitted white light. This is a recent account (2014) of an earlier observation (1998). The witness was 12 years old at the time. He is currently unable to determine the precise date and month of the observation (he indicated August on the questionnaire but suggested July as a possibility to the investigator). Under these circumstances, despite an interview with the witness, the scope of the investigation remains very limited. The hypothesis of a solar balloon (Piff Gadget type) is plausible due to its shape and silent movement, and addresses the core of the strangeness. However, it is impossible to verify the consistency of its direction of movement with the wind (see the investigation report). In conclusion, the case admits of a possible explanation, which, given the limited information, cannot be confirmed or refuted. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies it as C: lack of reliable information.

summary: Observation of distress flare firings
description: On July 19, 1998, around 11 p.m., several witnesses observed three red lights rising into the sky before slowly descending. One of these phenomena reportedly caused a fire. The investigation quickly revealed that it was caused by the firing of expired distress flares by a private individual.

summary: Observation by a motorist who had broken down of an object floating close to the ground and taking off vertically with three "beings" inside: lack of reliable information.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its website: www.cnes-geipan.fr. Its publications include older cases, classified at the time (A, B, C, or D), which are now being re-examined solely to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D, is part of a set of cases recently re-examined. On the night of June 27-28, 1998, around 1:00 AM, a motorist suddenly experienced a total vehicle breakdown (engine, headlights, and radio stopped working). He pulled over to the side of the road and then noticed a green glow in front of his vehicle. The witness gets out of the vehicle and approaches, but feels paralyzed. He then observes a stationary conical object floating above the ground and a being moving towards the interior of the object, which has three seats, two of which are occupied. The object then quickly takes off vertically. The witness, gradually regaining his composure, gets back into his vehicle. The next day, the witness realizes he has a significant memory gap regarding some of what he did the previous evening. He returns to the site accompanied, but no trace is visible. Only one witness statement is recorded. The local police found no trace or clue. The current witness statement is extremely strange: - a wingless conical craft, floating above the ground and taking off vertically; - small men with oval heads and four fingers entering the craft via a gangplank before takeoff. The case was then classified as Class D. However, according to GEIPAN's current methodology (see GEIPAN's Classification Methodology), this classification is incorrect. The consistency of the testimony is insufficient to validate an unexplained or inexplicable nature. In terms of information, a second independent witness and/or indisputable evidence (photos or traces on the ground) would have been necessary. Reliability is also an issue, as the witness does not remember what they did in the four hours preceding this observation. Therefore, one might wonder if this observation is not the result of another type of memory distortion. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as Class C: unusable testimony.

summary: Observing white glimmers through a skylight
description: On the night of June 17-18, 1998, a woman in her bathroom saw three white lights in the sky through her skylight for about ten minutes. She took three photos. The photos were unusable. The phenomenon could not be analyzed.

summary: Likely re-entry of space debris
description: On April 23, 1998, at 3:38 a.m., the pilot of a Boeing 727 en route to Barcelona observed, in the distance, the passage of very fast blue and green lights that disappeared in an explosion. This was probably the atmospheric reentry of a piece of space debris.

summary: Close observation of the silent passage of a dark, round craft; presence of two men in the cockpit: recent testimony of an old sighting without a current date: lack of information and cross-checks.
description: Recent testimony (October 18, 2013) of an old sighting. In April 1998 (the witness no longer remembers the exact date; the date is arbitrary), around 2 p.m., a witness in front of her vacation home was startled by a persistent shadow above her. Looking up, she observed a round, black craft moving slowly and silently just above the house. The craft hovered in front of the witness, 3 or 4 meters above the ground, and the witness saw two men in a cockpit, "fairly young, one behind the other, wearing simple white helmets without visors." The craft then moved off again over the trees, heading west. No other testimonies have been collected. This testimony of a close, and therefore strange, sighting was only reported to GEIPAN more than 15 years after the events, which implies a significant risk of false, or at least partial, recollections. Furthermore, the precise date of the observation is unknown, preventing any comparison with other similar cases. Due to a lack of precise information, GEIPAN classifies this case as "C".

summary: Observation of a black object flying in the sky: observation of a kite in flight.
description: On February 8, 1998, at approximately 3:00 PM, a witness reported seeing a black object in the sky. The investigation quickly revealed that the witness had observed the kite used that same day by a professional photographer to take aerial photographs. A demonstration was given to the witness, who confirmed that the kite matched what he had seen.

summary: Observation of a rocket-shaped object moving horizontally.
description: On February 6, 1998, at approximately 4:00 PM, a man chopping wood observed a rocket-like object moving across the sky with a low rumbling sound. No further information is available.

summary: Two sightings of unidentified objects
description: On January 17, 1998, three passengers in the same car observed a "shining shell" 20 to 25 meters in diameter with black stripes and several bright points or yellow and red lights. This sighting was reported in a newspaper article, but the witnesses could not be identified or interviewed. Following the first article, a fourth witness came forward to report a similar phenomenon on January 21, 1998, around 6:30 p.m. While in her car, she observed a luminous disc twice the size of the Moon for about twenty seconds. These various brief and somewhat contradictory accounts do not allow for a serious analysis of the observed phenomena.

summary: Instrumental observation of a point of light in the sky.
description: On January 6, 1998, an amateur astronomer observed the sky and filmed a bright point with his telescope, seemingly moving across the sky, as shown in the recording. No further information is available.
